about: Checking a Show of a book after the first of its permission (format description, sections 11, 21.6 and 29), on a device without SLH-DSA.

cases.name: a Show of book 2 with its first seal among the pages, not every page it covers

notes: The top fingerprint was not compared with a copy you already trust, and no seal with a time-stamp from a service you trust comes with it.
Single pages cannot show whether the chain is whole, whether a limit was kept, or whether an approval was used only once. Those need every stub under the slip.
Single pages cannot show that a slip was not cancelled, or that a vouching record was not withdrawn, on a page that is not shown.

content.purpose: Keep the office stocked with paper, pens and toner.

notes: This seal is shown as a single page. It could not be compared with the entries before it, so its time-stamp is not taken to show when any other page existed. Its dates are still held against the pages that come before it in the book.

The statements beside this seal from witnesses you trust were not counted: the pages do not hold every entry this seal covers, and single pages cannot show that every permission among them is from the passkey and for the agent of the permission the book starts from. A witness knows a book only by the passkey and the agent of the permission it starts from and the keys of its recorder, which the recorder chooses, so a statement counts only for a book that starts with a permission signed by a passkey you named, sealed by a recorder you named.

limits: It shows what was recorded, not what was left out. An agent that acts and writes no stub leaves no trace here.
A one-sided stub shows what the agent's side said, not what the other side did.
A refusal shows what the service's side said, not what the agent did.
It does not show that an action was wise, lawful or wanted.
A rule of conduct in a slip, such as "never claim to be a human being", is the person's signed instruction. No check can show that the agent kept it.
It does not show who was holding the device when the passkey signed.
A name in a record is a label. Only keys are checked.

Nothing here is time-stamped by an outside service that you named as trusted. So it does not show when the record was made, and the latest stubs under a slip or a pass, or a slip or a pass with all its stubs, could have been removed.

A witness you named as trusted signed for the seal at entry 2, which covers the first 2 entries. This book starts from a permission signed by a passkey you named, every permission before the seal is from that passkey for the same agent, and the book is sealed by a recorder you named. For that recorder, that passkey and the agent the permission names, the witness states that it saw this seal, and that it will sign for no seal that does not extend it, in this book or a later one, whichever permission from that passkey to that agent the book starts from. So a second history of those entries, sealed by the same recorder and starting from a permission that passkey gave that agent, shown to someone else, would need that witness to sign for it too. It does not cover a history sealed with other keys, even keys you also named, nor one that starts from a permission for another agent. It does not show when the seal was made, that nothing was cut off after a later seal, nor anything never shown to the witness: to see whether the end of the book is missing, ask the witness for the latest seal it holds for this recorder, passkey and agent, and hand that seal over beside the book it is of. These are single pages of a book: they cannot show that a limit over the whole book was kept (section 11), so being witnessed says nothing here about totals.
